streetContent.description:
Gowland Crescent is a residential curve in Milton's Timberlea neighbourhood, the kind of street that bends back on itself and keeps its traffic local. It sits within a mature pocket of west Milton, framed by the parks and school grounds that give this part of town its shape. Sam Sherratt Trail Park is a short walk away, and the surrounding streets carry the quiet rhythm of a settled residential grid. The crescent's position puts it within easy reach of the grocery and retail cluster along the main commercial corridors, while keeping the immediate surroundings residential. For anyone learning the geography of Timberlea, Gowland is a small but representative piece of it.

The housing stock on Gowland Crescent is detached, and detached only. Three detached homes appear in the recent record, with no semi, townhouse, or condo activity alongside them. That single-type profile gives the street a consistent built character from end to end. One active listing is present. Across the wider Timberlea area, detached homes typically trade around $1.05M, a figure that situates this pocket in Milton's mid-tier detached market. The street itself carries too few recent sales to publish its own range, so the neighbourhood figure is the more reliable reference point for the area's detached tier.

Daily life on Gowland Crescent leans on a compact set of nearby anchors. Sam Sherratt Trail Park is under a minute's walk, and Beaver Court Park follows at about two minutes on foot. Moorelands Park and Sam Sherratt Park are each roughly four minutes away, giving the immediate area an unusual density of green space for a residential pocket. Grocery runs are short drives: Canadian Superstore and Sobeys Milton both sit about four minutes out, with Walmart and FreshCo a minute further. Milton District Hospital is a five-minute drive, and the on-ramp to Highway 401 at James Snow Parkway is about the same.

Schools are close without being on the doorstep. Sam Sherratt PS is a four-minute drive, and Anne J. MacArthur PS, Irma Coulson PS, and Robert Baldwin PS are each about five minutes out. On the Catholic side, Guardian Angels, Holy Rosary, and St. Anthony of Padua elementary schools sit at roughly five minutes, with Bishop P.F. Reding Catholic SS at the same distance. The Milton Muslim Community Centre is a five-minute drive, and the Halton Islamic Community Centre about ten. Milton GO Station is ten minutes away, which shapes the commute for anyone heading into Toronto.

Gowland Crescent trades rarely, and the record over the past year is thin enough that no street-level price range can be published with confidence. What the data does show is a street of detached homes, and only detached homes, with three recorded sales and three recorded leases across the window. One active listing sits on the market at present. That is the whole of the supply picture: a single property available, against a street where turnover is genuinely low. Days on market cannot be stated for the street itself, since the sale count falls below the threshold at which a pace figure becomes meaningful.

The clearest pricing reference for Gowland Crescent is therefore the wider Timberlea neighbourhood, where comparable detached homes have been trading around $1.05M. That neighbourhood read carries a substantial sample and a sold-to-ask figure just under parity, which points to modest negotiation room rather than either a bidding premium or heavy discounting. On the rental side, three-bedroom homes on the street typically rent around $2,800 a month, drawn from a small pool of leases. The street sits within walking distance of Sam Sherratt Trail Park and Beaver Court Park, with Milton District Hospital and the James Snow Parkway interchange both a short drive out. Suitability questions belong elsewhere on this page; the market read here is simply that Gowland Crescent is a low-turnover detached street whose pricing is clearest when read against the neighbourhood comparable.

Across Timberlea, comparable detached homes have sold at broadly similar levels, and the neighbourhood read is the more reliable of the two scopes given how infrequently Gowland Crescent itself changes hands. The typical sold price for detached homes in the neighbourhood sits around $1.05M, drawn from a deep sample of recent sales rather than a handful of trades. Sold-to-ask sits just below parity, which implies a market where modest negotiation is normal and buyers are not routinely paying above asking. Neighbourhood-wide, comparable detached homes typically clear in around 89 days, a pace that reflects a measured market rather than a rushed one. Year-over-year direction is not published for this scope, so no trend claim is made here. Taken together, the neighbourhood picture is one of steady, unhurried trade at a level that anchors what a detached home in this part of Milton has been worth.

Gowland Crescent sits in Timberlea, a position that makes the GO station the realistic Toronto commute; the walk to Milton GO Station runs about ten minutes, and from there the train and subway combination reaches downtown in roughly seventy minutes. By car the street is well placed for the western GTA. The 401 onramp at James Snow Parkway is a five-minute drive, which puts Mississauga around twenty-two minutes and Oakville around twenty-four, with Burlington a touch closer at twenty. Pearson runs about thirty-two minutes in typical traffic. The pattern here is a street that trades a longer rail commute for quick highway access, and the two together cover most of what the western corridor asks for.

Sam Sherratt PS is the nearest Halton District School Board elementary, about four minutes on foot, with Anne J. MacArthur PS, Irma Coulson PS and Robert Baldwin PS each roughly five minutes away. On the Catholic side, Guardian Angels Catholic ES, Holy Rosary Catholic ES and St. Anthony of Padua Catholic ES all sit about five minutes by car, and Bishop P.F. Reding Catholic SS is the closest secondary option at a similar distance. The cluster is tight enough that most of these are a short walk or a quick drive rather than a cross-town trip. School assignment should be confirmed with the boards directly.

If the priorities sit elsewhere, two nearby streets frame the alternatives. Fox Crescent, in Dempsey, carries detached homes trading around $1.15M, a step above the Timberlea detached band. Tupper Drive, in Clarke, runs to townhouse product trading around $975K, which trades space for a lower entry point. The difference is largely one of housing mix and price tier rather than location, since all three sit within a few minutes of the same highway and GO access. A buyer weighing lot size against finished square footage will find the tradeoffs land differently on each.
